title: Copy routine run
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $k$ be a copy site, and let $S$ be a machine state, $M\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ a memory configuration, and $p\in\mathbb{Z}$. If $0\le p\le P$, every register value of $S$ is at most $B$, its scratch register $Z$ is zero, and the sum of the source and destination register values for $k$ is at most $B$, then the machine has a finite guarded run from the first phase of the copy routine, initialized with $S$, memory $M$, and head position $p$, to the exit control state for $k$. At the endpoint, the destination register contains the sum of its initial value and the source register's initial value; all other registers, the memory, and the head position are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: Every register value of $S$ is at most $B$
The sum of the source and destination register values is at most $B$
